paper_title: DeltaEdit Enhancing Sequential Editing in Large Language Models by   Controlling Superimposed Noise
caption: The variation curve of k^⊤β for AlphaEdit and MEMIT as the number of edits increases, with GPT2-XL serving as the edited model. As the results of Llama3-8B are not suitable for display in a line chart, they are presented in Appendix <ref>.
model_annotation: The line chart illustrates the variation of the quantity k^⊤β for two editing methods—AlphaEdit and MEMIT—as the number of edits increases, using GPT2-XL as the target model. The x-axis represents the number of edits, ranging linearly from 0 to 3000 with tick marks at intervals of 500. The y-axis, labeled k^⊤β, spans from 0 to 0.012 with tick intervals of 0.002, and uses a linear scale. The AlphaEdit curve, shown in solid red with circular markers, begins at approximately 0.004 when the number of edits is 0, decreases to about 0.0028 at 500 edits, then continues to decline gradually to roughly 0.0015 by 3000 edits. The MEMIT curve, depicted in solid light blue with circular markers, starts at approximately 0.0045 at 0 edits, rises steadily to about 0.0055 at 500 edits, then increases more steeply to reach 0.013 at 3000 edits, showing a consistent upward trend across the entire range.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the variation of the quantity $ k^\top \beta $ for two editing methods—AlphaEdit (red line) and MEMIT (light blue line)—as the number of edits increases, with GPT2-XL as the target model. The x-axis, labeled with values ranging from approximately 0 to 3000, represents the number of edits, marked at intervals of 500 (500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, 3000), and appears to use a linear scale. The y-axis, labeled $ k^\top \beta $, spans from 0 to 0.014, with major grid lines at intervals of 0.002 (0.002, 0.004, ..., 0.014). The AlphaEdit curve, marked with circular red data points and a solid red line, begins at approximately 0.004 at 0 edits, drops sharply to about 0.0025 at 500 edits, then continues to decline gradually to roughly 0.001 at 3000 edits. In contrast, the MEMIT curve, marked with circular light blue data points and a solid light blue line, starts at about 0.0045 at 0 edits and increases monotonically, reaching approximately 0.013 at 3000 edits, with a visibly accelerating upward trend in the latter half of the x-axis.
